newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign-charged Polish zloty hits six-week high.
newsitem.headline: Foreign-charged Polish zloty hits six-week high.

text.p: The zloty climbed to a six-week high on Wednesday amid foreign entry into Polish treasuries and no central bank intervention against the surging local unit.
Dealers said the currency selling sentiment was caused by foreign entry into T-bills and domestic banks reducing currency exposure for higher yielding zloty positions over the week-end.

"Today's zloty buying was sparked by foreign purchases of T-bills and domestic players cutting positions to take advantage of the attractive high yielding zloty over the weekend," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 3.25/3.20 percent from the trading band centre, up from Tuesday's 3.17/3.13 percent, its highest level against the parity rate since February 19.
It closed at 3.1080/00 to the dollar, down from 3.1070/80 on Tuesday and at 1.8085/00 to the mark, up from 1.8120/30.

Dealers said the central bank likely refrained from staging a currency-buying intervention because it did not want to make Polish T-bills more attractive to speculative foreign capital ahead of Thursday's 500 million zloty auction.
But some said the central bank could intervene on Friday after payments for the Thursday auction had already been made.
Dealers expected the 52-week T-bill yield to hold steady around 21.90 percent or inch up on Thursday but said foreign investor demand was likely to be capped by the surging zloty.
On the money market one-day deposits dipped slightly but remained higher than the central bank's main drainge rate of 22.15 percent for 14-days.
Overnight depos closed at 22.70/23.30 percent, down from opening's 23.20/23.40 and tomorrow/next rates eased to 22.80/23.30 percent from Tuesday's 23.10/23.30 percent.
